analyzed_vuln.description: While reading the tag directory, `_cmsReadHeader` treats any later tag with the same offset and size as an internal link to the earlier tag, but does not verify that the two tag signatures have compatible tag types (despite the `// Check types.` comment). This permits a cooked object parsed according to one tag's descriptor to be stored in the linked target's slot. In this PoV, `cmsReadTag(gamt)` follows the attacker-created `gamt -> desc` link, validates/parses the shared `mft2` payload as a gamut LUT, and stores the resulting `cmsPipeline*` in the `desc` slot. During save, `SaveTags` handles that slot according to the `desc` descriptor and selects the MLU writer; `Type_MLU_Write` then interprets the pipeline as `cmsMLU` and reads beyond its allocation at cmstypes.c:1591. The root cause is the missing type-compatibility validation when `_cmsReadHeader` creates links, not bounds handling in `Type_MLU_Write`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A malformed ICC profile must contain two distinct tag signatures whose directory entries have identical nonzero, in-range offsets and sizes, causing the later entry to be linked to the earlier one, while their supported cooked types are incompatible. In this PoV the earlier tag is `desc`, the later tag is `gamt`, both reference offset 0x168 and size 0x84, and the shared bytes contain a valid `mft2`/LUT16 object. The harness opens the profile, calls `cmsReadTag(cmsSigGamutTag)`, which follows the link and places a parsed `cmsPipeline` into the `desc` slot, then calls `cmsSaveProfileToFile`. With the profile version causing `desc` to be emitted as multi-localized Unicode, the save path passes that pipeline to `Type_MLU_Write`, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow.

args: In lcms/src/cmsio0.c, what is the best project-consistent way for _cmsReadHeader to validate type compatibility before setting TagLinked for two directory entries with identical offset and size? Please inspect relevant descriptor structures, helper declarations/order, plugin support, and upstream/history if recognizable. Should compatibility mean intersection of the two tag descriptors' SupportedTypes, or should the code read the shared on-disk base type and verify both descriptors support that exact type? Note that _cmsReadHeader is currently iterating the directory, so seeking into tag payload may disturb directory reading unless position is restored.

The reported vulnerability is that _cmsReadHeader at lcms/src/cmsio0.c lines 795-803 links any same-offset/same-size entries without implementing its 'Check types' comment. A crafted desc then gamt pair shares an mft2 payload. cmsReadTag(gamt) resolves the link to the desc slot and stores a cmsPipeline there; SaveTags later uses the desc descriptor and treats it as cmsMLU, causing an ASan heap overflow. I have confirmed cmsReadTag checks the requested signature against the payload base type, but because _cmsSearchTag follows the link, the cooked pointer lands in the earlier signature's slot. We need fix root cause, likely only create links where tag descriptors are compatible, while preserving legitimate ICC shared tag data and behavior for unknown/plugin descriptors.
